day_shape: CENTCOM marks 100 days of its Iran naval blockade claiming $25bn in blocked crude exports, Rubio reassures Qatar on Hormuz navigation, Khamenei warns 'new fronts will be opened', and IRGC reports four vessels struck in the Gulf.

threads.label: CENTCOM blockade hits 100-day mark
threads.summary: CENTCOM announced 100 days since resuming its naval blockade of Iran, claiming it has prevented at least $25 billion in crude exports with no non-humanitarian sea trade. Iran International reported collapsed LPG exports leaving surplus propane and butane, and Jerusalem Post cited floating oil reserves falling from 90 million barrels to zero.

threads.label: Hormuz, Gulf shipping and Rubio-Qatar call
threads.summary: Secretary Rubio spoke with Qatari PM Al Thani, reaffirming US commitment to Qatar's security and freedom of navigation through the Strait of Hormuz. The IRGC Navy said four vessels were struck in the Persian Gulf with three hitting mines in the Strait of Hormuz, and IRIB reported Brent crude above $113.

threads.label: Khamenei warns of new fronts, IRGC bomb
threads.summary: Khamenei's office posted a message saying studies have been conducted on opening 'new fronts' with activation should the war continue, echoed by IRIB. Jerusalem Post reported the IRGC announced preparations to unveil a 'Father of All Bombs' in response to US threats, while Trump said 'something' would happen 'soon'.

threads.label: Israeli election-timing Iran calculus
threads.summary: Jerusalem Post reported Israeli intelligence that Iran and proxies are considering attacks ahead of elections, while security officials warned the government against striking Iran now for fear of appearing to interfere. Netanyahu told the Post he wants more terms to 'break Iran's murderous regime'.

threads.label: IDF Gaza strikes and proxy linkages
threads.summary: The IDF said it killed Ramadan Muhammad Ashahada Diab, Khan Younis head of the Popular Resistance Committees, which it linked to Hamas, Hezbollah and the IRGC. Jerusalem Post also reported IAF strikes in northern Gaza and at least three killed per Hamas health officials, plus Hezbollah recruiting felons in Latin America.

threads.label: European sanctions and Iran plot trial
threads.summary: Germany's BaFin ordered liquidation of Bank Saderat Iran's Hamburg branch after revoking its licence, Greece said it is implementing Iran-linked sanctions, and Israel sanctioned UK-registered Coral Oil over alleged fuel supply to a Hezbollah firm. In London, a defendant said Iranian handlers instructed him to break an Iran International journalist's arms and legs.

threads.label: Yemen/Houthi Red Sea operations
threads.summary: Jerusalem Post reported Houthi claims of attacks on Saudi Arabia's defence ministry, Aramco facilities in Yanbu, and Dammam airport. Defa Press carried Yemeni Foreign Ministry statements condemning Saudi conduct in the Red Sea and images of Yemeni army attacks on Saudi-backed forces in Marib.

events.summary_en: Commander Jalali: Civil defence in war conditions requires scientific and people-centred review Head of the Organisation of Civil Defence of the country, emphasising that the country is not in normal and peaceful conditions, said: The enemy continues to act and threaten, and the issue of civil defence must be pursued at different dimensions and levels with a careful and scholarly perspective. Today's war is not just in the executive arena and on the streets; rather, spiritual, rescue and relief, covert and infrastructure layers also play a role in it. The continuation of electricity, gas, communications, health and treatment, and the provision of supplies needed by the people are the result of invisible actions and the efforts of anonymous fighters who work in the civil defence sector.
